messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [Name]

Age: 80 years

Sex: Male

Medical Record Number: [Number]

Date of Admission: [Date]

Date of Discharge: [Date]

Hospital Course:

The patient was admitted to our hospital due to the incidentally discovered rectal tumor. The biopsy sample revealed that the 3 cm diameter tumor was a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. Imaging studies showed that the tumor invaded into the muscularis propria, and lateral pelvic lymph nodes were not enlarged. The patient also had a huge benign prostatic hypertrophy, with a size of 85 × 80 × 70 mm.

To achieve complete tumor removal with negative margins, a hybrid transabdominal-transanal approach for ISR was performed. The procedure involved laparoscopic mobilization of the left colon and transabdominal approach up to the anterior dissection of the rectum. Subsequently, a transanal approach was used to complete the dissection procedure. The bilateral pelvic splanchnic nerves were identified at the 5 and 7 o’clock positions. Due to the perineal body and the enlarged prostate, the proper dissection layer at the anterior side was difficult to identify. However, the dissection plane between the rectum and the prostate was identified, and the procedure was completed along the same plane with the assistance of the laparoscopic approach.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and had an uneventful postoperative course. The patient was discharged home on [Date] with scheduled follow-up appointments.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Plan:

The patient is advised to follow-up with his oncologist and urologist for monitoring and further treatment as per their recommendations. The patient is also advised to make diet changes and exercise regularly to maintain good health.

Clinician:

[Name], [Title]

Attending Physician:

[Name], [Title]

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The admission was for intersphincteric resection of a biopsy-proven moderately differentiated rectal adenocarcinoma, a malignant neoplasm of the rectum. The prostatic hypertrophy is a comorbidity that only made the dissection harder. Malignant neoplasms are in chapter C, and the rectum category is C20.
CODE: C20
